# Power analysis {#sec-power} We want to investiguate what is the minimal interaction that can be detected with a maximum error of 10% with such experimental design with 4 replicates and with simulated data following a Poisson distribution (reproduction data are count data). We get the information about the experimental design. ::: {.cell code-show='show'} ```{.r .cell-code} df_design <- read.csv(here::here("data/Design_mixture.csv")) df_drc_param <- read.csv(here::here("data/DRC_parameters_cocoons_really_used.csv")) slope <- df_drc_param$coef.drc.4.[1] Y_max <- df_drc_param$coef.drc.4.[2] EPX_EC50 <- df_drc_param$coef.drc.4.[3] IMD_EC50 <- df_drc_param$coef.drc.4.[4] y_min <- 0 C_mat <- cbind(df_design$EPX, df_design$IMD) Max <- Y_max Slopes <- c(slope, slope) Ec50s <- c(EPX_EC50, IMD_EC50) ``` ::: For each reference model, we create a function that will simulate the response of `Nb_pop` experiments consisting of our experimental design with `Nb_rep` replicates for an exposure to a mixture with each of the interaction parameter value ($a$) contained in the list `l_interaction_a`. The interaction will then be estimated with the Jonker simple interaction model and categorized as significant or non-significant (Log-Likelihood ratio test against the nulle model). Due to the high computational requirements, these functions were executed on the calculation servers (CCRT) of the CEA (Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives, a french research organisation). ::: {.cell code-show='show'} ```{.r .cell-code} f_power_design_CA <- function(Nb_rep, l_interaction_a, Nb_pop, param){ res <- data.frame() for (Nb_rep_j in Nb_rep){ for (interaction_a_i in l_interaction_a){ print(interaction_a_i) a_i <- interaction_a_i # Calculation of the theorical response res_CA_theorical_design_i <- CA_complete2( C_mat, Max, Slopes, Ec50s, interact="SA", a=a_i ) # We add the corresponding response to our design df_dose_rep_i <- df_design%>% mutate(rep_Y=res_CA_theorical_design_i) df_dose_rep_i <- df_dose_rep_i[,-c(1, 4)] for(k in 1:Nb_pop){ set.seed(121212+k) ID_pop <- k # Population simulation df_sim_data_k <- data.frame( Y=c(), EPX=c(), IMD=c() ) for(i in 1:length(df_dose_rep_i$EPX)){ Y_th <- df_dose_rep_i$rep_Y[i] Y_sim <- rpois(Nb_rep_j, Y_th) # <1> EPX <- rep(df_dose_rep_i$EPX[i], Nb_rep_j) IMD <- rep(df_dose_rep_i$IMD[i], Nb_rep_j) df_sim_data_j <- data.frame( Y_th=rep(Y_th, Nb_rep_j), Y_sim=Y_sim, EPX=EPX, IMD=IMD ) df_sim_data_k <- rbind(df_sim_data_k, df_sim_data_j) } # CA model res_CA_LL_k <- CA_complete2_Poisson( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact="none", Max = Max, Slopes = Slopes, Ec50s = Ec50s ) # Fit of the model SA res_CA_SA_fit_k<-CA_complete2_fit_speed( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact="SA", param=param, error_type = "Poisson" ) res_a_k <- res_CA_SA_fit_k$a res_CA_SA_LL_k <- CA_complete2_Poisson( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact= "SA", a = res_a_k, Max = Max, Slopes = Slopes, Ec50s = Ec50s ) # LL ratio test LL0 <- res_CA_LL_k LL1 <- res_CA_SA_LL_k p0 <- 0 p1 <- 1 D <- -2 * (LL1 - LL0) p_val_k <- pchisq(D, df = p1 - p0, lower.tail = FALSE) Signif_k <- (p_val_k <= 0.05) res_k <- data.frame( Simulated_interaction = a_i, Estimated_interaction = res_a_k, p_val = p_val_k, Signif = Signif_k, ID_pop = ID_pop, Nb_rep = Nb_rep_j ) res <- rbind(res, res_k) } #print("Calculations done for given interaction") } #print("Calculations done for given Nb_rep") } return(res) } f_power_design_IA <- function(Nb_rep, l_interaction_a, Nb_pop, param){ res <- data.frame() for (Nb_rep_j in Nb_rep){ for (interaction_a_i in l_interaction_a){ print(interaction_a_i) a_i <- interaction_a_i # Calculation of the theorical response res_IA_theorical_design_i <- IA_complete2( C_mat, Max, Slopes, Ec50s, interact="SA", a=a_i ) # We add the corresponding response to our design df_dose_rep_i <- df_design%>% mutate(rep_Y=res_IA_theorical_design_i) df_dose_rep_i <- df_dose_rep_i[,-c(1, 4)] for(k in 1:Nb_pop){ set.seed(121212+k) ID_pop <- k # Population simulation df_sim_data_k <- data.frame( Y=c(), EPX=c(), IMD=c() ) for(i in 1:length(df_dose_rep_i$EPX)){ Y_th <- df_dose_rep_i$rep_Y[i] Y_sim <- rpois(Nb_rep_j, Y_th) # <1> EPX <- rep(df_dose_rep_i$EPX[i], Nb_rep_j) IMD <- rep(df_dose_rep_i$IMD[i], Nb_rep_j) df_sim_data_j <- data.frame( Y_th=rep(Y_th, Nb_rep_j), Y_sim=Y_sim, EPX=EPX, IMD=IMD ) df_sim_data_k <- rbind(df_sim_data_k, df_sim_data_j) } # IA model res_IA_LL_k <- IA_complete2_Poisson( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact="none", Max = Max, Slopes = Slopes, Ec50s = Ec50s ) # Fit of the model SA res_IA_SA_fit_k<-IA_complete_fit_speed( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact="SA", param=param, error_type = "Poisson" ) res_a_k <- res_IA_SA_fit_k$a res_IA_SA_LL_k <- IA_complete2_Poisson( C_mat=cbind( df_sim_data_k$EPX, df_sim_data_k$IMD ), Response=df_sim_data_k$Y_sim, interact= "SA", a = res_a_k, Max = Max, Slopes = Slopes, Ec50s = Ec50s ) # LL ratio test LL0 <- res_IA_LL_k LL1 <- res_IA_SA_LL_k p0 <- 0 p1 <- 1 D <- -2 * (LL1 - LL0) p_val_k <- pchisq(D, df = p1 - p0, lower.tail = FALSE) Signif_k <- (p_val_k <= 0.05) res_k <- data.frame( Simulated_interaction = a_i, Estimated_interaction = res_a_k, p_val = p_val_k, Signif = Signif_k, ID_pop = ID_pop, Nb_rep = Nb_rep_j ) res <- rbind(res, res_k) } #print("Calculations done for given interaction") } #print("Calculations done for given Nb_rep") } return(res) } ``` ::: ### With CA as reference ::: {.cell code-show='show'} ```{.r .cell-code} Nb_rep <- c(4) tmp <- c(10, 7, 5, 2, 1, 0.5, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001) l_interaction_a <- c(tmp, -rev(tmp)) Nb_pop <- 5000 # df_boot_res_CA <- f_power_design_CA(Nb_rep, l_interaction_a, Nb_pop, param) # save(df_boot_res_CA,file = here::here("mod/MIX/Res_boot_design_CA.RData")) load(file = here::here("mod/MIX/Res_boot_design_CA.RData")) l_interaction_a_ordered <- as.vector(rbind(tmp, -tmp)) df_boot_res_CA <- df_boot_res_CA |> mutate( Simulated_interaction_f = factor( Simulated_interaction, levels = l_interaction_a_ordered ) ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df_boot_res_CA_print <- df_boot_res_CA |> mutate( Per_error = round((Estimated_interaction - Simulated_interaction) / Simulated_interaction * 100, 5), Estimated_interaction = round(Estimated_interaction, 5), Error = Estimated_interaction - Simulated_interaction ) df_boot_res_CA_line <- data.frame( Simulated_interaction = l_interaction_a, Line = l_interaction_a ) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(bayestestR) f_pdir <- function(df) { Nb_rep_unique <- unique(df$Nb_rep) Simulated_interaction_unique <- unique(df$Simulated_interaction) res <- data.frame( Nb_rep = c(), Simulated_interaction = c(), P_direction = c() ) for (Nb_rep_i in Nb_rep_unique) { for (Simulated_interaction_i in Simulated_interaction_unique) { p_dir <- p_direction(subset(df, Nb_rep == Nb_rep_i & Simulated_interaction == Simulated_interaction_i)$Estimated_interaction) res_i <- data.frame( Nb_rep = Nb_rep_i, Simulated_interaction = Simulated_interaction_i, P_direction = p_dir[2] ) res <- rbind(res, res_i) } } return(res) } df_boot_res_CA_pdir <- f_pdir(df_boot_res_CA_print) df_boot_res_CA_line <- df_boot_res_CA_line |> left_join(df_boot_res_CA_pdir, by = join_by(Simulated_interaction)) df_boot_res_CA_line <- df_boot_res_CA_line |> mutate( Simulated_interaction_f = factor( Simulated_interaction, levels = l_interaction_a_ordered ) ) ``` ::: Thanks to this algorithm, we can estimate the density of error ``` ::: ::: Power analysis revealed clear thresholds in the ability of the simple interaction (SA) model to detect and quantify interactions. With CA as the reference model, interaction strengths of a ≈ 1 provided adequate power (\~97%) and acceptable estimation accuracy (\< 20% error), whereas performance degraded markedly at a = 0.5. Using IA as the reference yielded the same qualitative threshold: a ≈ 1 was the minimum interaction strength at which detection remained reasonably reliable, although power was lower (\~80%) than under CA. For both reference models, weaker interactions (a ≤ 0.5) led to insufficient power and poor estimation accuracy, making them difficult to detect or classify robustly. :::: {#collapseOne .accordion-collapse .collapse}
